modelNote: This lab models correctness decisions for the Apache ORC Java reader. Exact exception and recovery behavior can vary by library and version.

parts.label: Header
parts.detail: The ORC magic bytes identify the file.

parts.label: Row indexes
parts.detail: Optional positions and per-row-group statistics support seeking and pruning.

parts.label: Bloom filters
parts.detail: Optional per-row-group membership tests can reject more equality candidates.

parts.label: Column streams
parts.detail: Encoded and compressed values make up the stripe data.

parts.label: Stripe footer
parts.detail: The stream directory records each stream's kind, column, encoding, and length.

parts.label: File tail
parts.detail: Metadata, footer, and postscript locate stripes and define schema and compression.

policies.label: Strict reader
policies.detail: Keep the Java reader default: throw when corrupt data is encountered.

policies.label: Skip corrupt data
policies.detail: Model orc.skip.corrupt.data=true; partial output is possible and must be labeled.

scenarios.label: Healthy file
scenarios.detail: All required metadata and data streams are readable.

strict.explanation: The reader can locate every stream and use all available pruning metadata.

skip-corrupt.explanation: The permissive setting changes nothing because no corruption is present.

scenarios.label: Bloom filter not written
scenarios.detail: The writer did not configure a Bloom filter for the predicate column.

strict.explanation: Bloom filters are optional. The reader can still use min/max statistics, then apply the predicate to decoded rows.

skip-corrupt.explanation: No corrupt data is being skipped. Equality pruning may be less selective, but result completeness is unchanged.

scenarios.label: Row indexes disabled
scenarios.detail: The writer intentionally omitted row-group index streams.

strict.explanation: An ORC file can be read without row indexes. The reader loses row-group seeking and pruning inside a candidate stripe.

skip-corrupt.explanation: The indexes are absent by design, not corrupt. The permissive setting provides no additional benefit.

scenarios.label: Corrupt column stream
scenarios.detail: One encoded data stream cannot be decoded.

strict.explanation: The default Java setting throws instead of silently returning an incomplete result.

skip-corrupt.explanation: Skipping corrupt data can preserve some rows, but counts and aggregates are not complete unless another source repairs the gap.

scenarios.label: Damaged stripe footer
scenarios.detail: The reader cannot trust the stream directory for one stripe.

strict.explanation: Without the stripe footer, the reader cannot safely map stream bytes to columns and encodings.

skip-corrupt.explanation: A permissive data policy does not reconstruct a missing stream directory. Quarantine the file and use validation or recovery tooling.

scenarios.label: Truncated file tail
scenarios.detail: The postscript or file footer is incomplete.

strict.explanation: The reader cannot reliably locate stripes, recover the schema, or determine the compression settings.

skip-corrupt.explanation: Skipping corrupt row data cannot replace the top-level metadata needed to interpret the file.
